Row CV:def:record, declaration CV.record_definition : CV.RecordDefinitionData (statement file lines 342-400). Clause by clause, with source lines from the excerpt (= d1_setup.tex 522-551) and Lean lines from work/reviews/cv-record-homfly-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt.

(1) "A record consists of an oriented circle Γ; a finite subset V ⊂ Γ of marked points; a partition of V into two-element sets, the double points; for each double point a designation of one of its two points as the over position and the other as the under position; and for each double point a sign in {±1}" (excerpt 2-6) -> field `record` (351-355) on every `ρ : Record` with `SingleCircle ρ` (130: `ρ.componentCount = 1`, i.e. `Fintype.card ρ.comps = 1`, LinkRecord.lean 350). Expansion: `Record` (LinkRecord.lean 309-338) has finite `M` (`mFin`), `succ : Perm M` with `succ_cycle : comp v = comp w → succ.SameCycle v w`, `pair : Perm M` with `pair_ne`, `pair_invol`, `isOver : M → Bool` with `bit_pair`, `sgn : M → SignType` with `sgn_pair`, `sgn_ne`. With one circle, `comp` is constant so `succ` is one cycle through all of `M` (`SingleCircle.sameCycle`, 137-140): this is the successor encoding of "V sits on one oriented circle"; the cyclic order of V is the orbit order of `succ`. `Crossing = {p : Finset M // ∃ v, p = {v, pair v}}` (LinkRecord 461); `x.1.card = 2` (`pair_ne`) and `∀ v, ∃! x, v ∈ x.1` (`crossingOf`, `crossingOf_eq_iff`, LinkRecord 467, 485) together are exactly a partition of V into two-element sets. `isOver (pair v) = !isOver v` is exactly "one of its two points over, the other under". `sgn (pair v) = sgn v ∧ (sgn v = 1 ∨ sgn v = -1)` is exactly one sign in {±1} per double point. Nothing of the printed data is absent; the abstract circle Γ is not carried as an object, only its cyclic order on V — the printed paragraph 21-27 itself says an isomorphism sees nothing of Γ beyond that (extension determined up to isotopy by the cyclic-order-preserving bijection), and for |V| ≥ 3 cyclic order and successor determine each other while for |V| ≤ 2 both are trivial. Judged a faithful encoding (non-blocking note recorded).

(2) "The record of a link diagram is the one obtained by taking Γ to be its traversal circle, V the preimages of its crossings, the partition the crossing correspondence, and the over/under and sign data those of the diagram" (excerpt 6-9) -> field `diagram_record` (364-371), for every `D : Diagram`. Expansion of `Diagram.record` (LinkDiagramRecord.lean 500-514, an `abbrev`): `comps = Fin D.Γ.c` (one circle when `componentCount = D.Γ.c = 1`, LinkDiagram 580; `singleCircle_record` 148-151), `M = D.Γ.Visit = Σ x : Crossing, {s // s ∈ x.val}` (LinkDiagram 256; a crossing together with the strand passing through it, i.e. one of its two preimages — Generic (LinkDiagram 394-400) gives transversality and no triple points so a crossing has exactly two), `succ v = nextVisit v` (258-259: cyclic `List.next` on the component's occurrences sorted by `visitCoord = traversalKey (visitPt v).2 ∈ [0,k)`, 181, 1435-1437), pinned by `¬ VisitBetween v u (succ v)` for all u on the component (`nextVisit_no_between` 335) — with the one-cycle clause of `record` this is exactly the next marked point along the oriented traversal circle; `pair v = twin v` with `(twin v).1 = v.1` (413: the other strand of the same crossing = the crossing correspondence); `isOver v = true ↔ v.2.val = overStrand v.1` (470, 627: the over position is the passage on the chosen over strand); `sgn v = D.sign v.1 = SignType.sign (det (dir overStrand) (dir underStrand))` (LinkDiagram 552-553) — the same convention as CV's det(u_over,u_under) > 0 ⇔ positive (d1_setup.tex 570-572). Faithful.

(3) "A record isomorphism … is a bijection φ : V → V′ that (a) preserves the cyclic order …; (b) carries double points to double points; (c) carries over positions to over positions and under to under; (d) preserves signs" (excerpt 11-20) -> definitions `PreservesCyclicOrder` (158-159: `∀ v w u, D.VisitBetween v w u → D'.VisitBetween (Φ v) (Φ w) (Φ u)`, one-directional as printed; `VisitBetween v w u := cycBetween (coord v) (coord w) (coord u)`, `cycBetween a b c := (a<b<c) ∨ (b<c<a) ∨ (c<a<b)`, LinkDiagramRecord 78-79, 882-883, which is definitionally the accepted `traversalBetween`, 81-83: "v,w,u occur in that cyclic order on the oriented traversal circle"), `CarriesDoublePoints` (163-164: image of every `{v, pair v}` is a double point of ρ′ — literal (b)), `CarriesOverUnder` (167-169: over ↦ over and under ↦ under — literal (c)), and `IsRecordIsoData` (272-280: (a),(b),(c) plus `signs : ∀ v, sgn' (Φ v) = sgn v` — (d)). Field `iso` (376-378): every SM `RecordIso ρ ρ'` (LinkRecord 539-552: `e : comps ≃ comps'`, `Φ : M ≃ M'`, `comp_eq`, `succ_eq`, `pair_eq`, `bit_eq`, `sgn_eq`) yields a bijection with (b),(c),(d) and successor commutation. Field `iso_iff` (383-385 = `recordIso_iff` 321-325): for one-component `D`, `D'`, a bijection `Φ : D.Γ.Visit ≃ D'.Γ.Visit` satisfies (a)-(d) iff it is the `Φ` of some `RecordIso D.record D'.record` (whose `e : Fin 1 ≃ Fin 1` is unique). So on CV's domain CV's record isomorphism is exactly SM's named record isomorphism; the printed clauses are rendered literally. The restriction to one-component diagrams is CV's domain (def:diagrammatic 315-344 and def:piecediagram 565-575 speak of one polygon P and its traversal circle; the docstring's citation of d10_axioms 525-531 is outside my permitted reading and was not verified). Faithful; the one residual (abstract records not of a Diagram get (a) only in the successor form) is recorded as non-blocking.

(4) "Condition (a) says exactly that φ extends to an orientation-preserving homeomorphism Γ → Γ′ carrying V onto V′, and any two such extensions are isotopic through such homeomorphisms: [proof sketch]" (excerpt 21-27) -> field `extension` (390): every `RecordIso D.record D'.record` satisfies `ExtendsToCircleMaps` (LinkDiagramRecord 1174-1177: ∃ bijections `φ i` of the `TraversalPoint` circles of the components onto those of `ι.e i`, preserving `traversalBetween` (a cyclic-order-preserving bijection of the parameter circle [0,k) — the combinatorial stand-in for "orientation-preserving homeomorphism"), with `⟨ι.e (visitPt v).1, φ _ (visitPt v).2⟩ = visitPt (ι.Φ v)`, i.e. extending φ and carrying V onto V′). Rendered: the forward direction (isomorphism ⇒ extension) for one-component diagram records via iso_iff. Not rendered: the converse of "says exactly" (extension ⇒ (a), an immediate restriction fact), and the sentence "any two such extensions are isotopic through such homeomorphisms" with its proof sketch. I judge this sentence a justification of clause (a), not a definitional clause: it opens with "Condition (a) says exactly that …", it is followed by a colon and a proof sketch, it defines no notion, and no later clause of the definition (isomorphic, equivalence) depends on it. Weaker than source, non-blocking; the docstring (76-81) discloses it.

(5) "Records are isomorphic when such a φ exists; the relation is an equivalence" (excerpt 27-28) -> `Isomorphic ρ ρ' := Nonempty (RecordIso ρ ρ')` (330) and field `equivalence : Equivalence Isomorphic` (392, `isomorphic_equivalence` 333-336 via `RecordIso.refl/symm/trans`, LinkRecord 559-595). On one-component diagram records `Nonempty (RecordIso …)` is exactly "∃ φ with (a)-(d)" by iso_iff. Faithful.
